Lecture 2 App ML1 1 / 10Outline
1Modelling non-linearities
Lecture 2 App ML1 2 / 10Section 1
Modelling non-linearities
Lecture 2 App ML1 3 / 10Linear Models
Given a Linear Model:
y=β0+β1·x1+β2·x2+ε
This model is said to be linear because it is linear in its coefficients. Indeed, the following is a
Linear Model.
y=β0+β1·x1+β2·x2
1+β3·log(x2) +ε
Lecture 2 App ML1 4 / 10Linear Models
A model such as:
y=β0+β1·x1+β2·x12+β3·log(x2) +ε
CAN model non-linear relationships. In Rthis model would be fitted as:
lm.non.lin.1 <- lm(y ~ x_1 + I(x_1^2) + log(x_2), data = someData)
Lecture 2 App ML1 5 / 10Non-linear relationships
By including polynomials (e.g. x1+x12) we can model non-linear relationships with a Linear
Model.
This is also true for extensions of the Linear Model such as Generalised Linear Models.
Lecture 2 App ML1 6 / 10Non-linear effects
Linear models can model non-linear effects
e.g. by adding quadratic terms
y=β0+β1·x+β2·x2+ε
non-linear models are non-linear in their coefficients:
y=β0+β1·xβ2+ε
Lecture 2 App ML1 7 / 10Generalise Additive Models
In alternative to polynomials we can use GAMs, which are an extension of the Linear Model.
Lecture 2 App ML1 8 / 10Generalise Additive Models
GAMs come with advantages and disadvantages compared to e.g. polynomials. Here a very
short selection of the most practice-relevant ones:
+ the degree of complexity must NOT be set by the user
+ the ”estimated degrees of freedom” gives the user an indication of the complexity of a
given smooth term
+ smooth terms can be visualised
−GAMs can run into computational issues (e.g. models that do not converge)
−the use of a quadratic term is simpler to explain than a GAM to a non-technical audience
−in order to fit and understand the results of a GAM some technical knowledge is
required... and GAMs are a complex topic
Lecture 2 App ML1 9 / 10Must know for a Data Scientist
A widespread wrong myth in data science is
”... we don’t use Linear Models (or their extensions) because they cannot deal with non-linear
relationships”
This is wrong!
Linear Models CAN MODEL NON-LINEAR RELATIONSHIPS.
